chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dharih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, the one of good character/manners has a reward like that of the fasting one who stands (in prayer).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for having good manners in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni places this hadith within the chapter on good manners, underscoring the Shia emphasis that ethical conduct (akhlaq) is not merely social etiquette but a profound act of worship. By equating the reward of good character with the combined merit of fasting and night prayer, the Imam highlights that consistent moral excellence is as spiritually demanding and rewarding as rigorous ritual devotion. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the perfection of the self (tazkiyah) is intrinsically linked to outward behavior.
